chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muhammad from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

«The obligatory Tawaf: if you add to it an amount equal to the prayer, then if you add to that, you must repeat it; and likewise the Sa'i». And as for that which indicates that if one adds [circuits] while forgetful, it is not obligatory upon him to repeat the Sa'i, is what he narrated:

key_terms.السَّعْيُ: Sa'i, the ritual walking between Safa and Marwah
key_terms.الطَّوَافُ: Tawaf, the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba
key_terms.سَاهِياً: Forgetfully / while in a state of forgetfulness

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on adding extra circuits to Tawaf in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to define the threshold for invalidating Tawaf through excessive addition, equating the penalty to that of adding a full prayer cycle. This establishes a precise legal boundary for the validity of the pilgrimage rites, distinguishing between intentional excess requiring repetition and unintentional error. The text sets the stage for contrasting this strict liability with the leniency granted for forgetfulness (sahw) in the subsequent narration.
